speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 像你或我这样的工程师正在用智能体创建更多代码,这些智能体推送更多代码,而我们大多数人都在并行运行多个智能体,这推送的代码量就大得多了。

zh: GitHub 显然在艰难跟上,并且频繁宕机。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And Tomasz revealed Git hosting for the agentic era from scratch.
zh: Tomasz 从零开始为智能体时代重新设计了 Git 托管。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And this allows for fleets of agents to push in parallel.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: When GitHub is down, you can still keep working and you don't even need to migrate away from GitHub.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Entire captures all the prompt history with your agent right inside of the repo, easy to check back.
zh: Entire 把所有与智能体的提示词历史直接捕获在仓库内部,方便回查。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's got a pretty innovative UI to show all of this.

speaker: Unknown

en: Living in the UK,

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: The UK was a bit more of a spectrum and BBC market, whereas the US, the Commodores and the Ataris and things were a bit bigger.
zh: 英国更像是一个 Spectrum 和 BBC 的市场,而在美国,Commodore 和 Atari 之类的要更大一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that sort of got me a bit interested.
zh: 所以这让我产生了些兴趣。

en: And then I always sort of stayed interested in it.
zh: 然后我一直保持对它的兴趣。

en: I did the very boring thing.

speaker: Unknown
en: I went to uni.

en: I did a software engineering degree at a place called Demontford University, which the running joke in my family is it's in the top five universities in the Leicester area.

speaker: Unknown
en: There are only two universities in Leicester.

en: It was, I mean, it was, I loved it.

en: Sandwich course.

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: It meant there was much focus going in.

zh: 我当时为一家公司做工作,那时候他们叫 GEC Alstom。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was called Alstom.
zh: 那家公司叫 Alstom。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we did software for the European Space Agency and gas and steam turbines.
zh: 我们为欧洲航天局以及燃气轮机和蒸汽轮机做软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, really cool.
zh: 对,非常酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: I joined about the first time at that, and then I went back after.
zh: 我第一次就是在那里入职的,然后后来又回去了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when I went back, it was just around the time the first .com boom.
zh: 而我回去的时候,正好是第一次 .com 热潮前后。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so everybody left.
zh: 于是所有人都离职了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I went from being the person that was doing like nothing to the person did everything.
zh: 所以我从一个什么都不做的人变成了什么都要做的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I remember my first week there, I was given a Fortran 77 code base.
zh: 但我记得我在那里的第一周,我被交给了一个 Fortran 77 代码库。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Fortran 77 was released in the year I was born.
zh: Fortran 77 是在我出生那一年发布的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And every single for loop had a break condition because we were basically doing analysis on these Unix machines.
zh: 而每一个 for 循环都有一个中断条件,因为我们基本上是在这些 Unix 机器上做分析。

speaker: Unknown
en: If the models and the time on the machines was expensive and we were worried about accidental infinite loops, this is how I was trying to solve the halting problem basically.
zh: 如果模型和机器上的时间很昂贵,而我们担心意外的死循环,这基本上就是我试图解决停机问题的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So every for loop across these 8,000 files had a break condition of, I think it was 99,999 loops.
zh: 所以这 8,000 个文件里的每一个 for 循环都有一个中断条件,我记得是 99,999 次循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if it went over that, the program basically broke and aborted.
zh: 如果超过那个数,程序基本上就会出错并中止。

speaker: Unknown
en: The models had got bigger, the computer got more powerful, so it had to go through and change them more.
zh: 模型变大了,计算机变强了,所以不得不过去把它们改得更大。

speaker: Unknown
en: By hand back then.
zh: 那时候是手工改。

speaker: Unknown
en: By hand?
zh: 手工改?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, this is one of the nicest things that anyone's ever done to me in a professional career, because Fortran 77 is based on the old punch card limitations to an extent.
zh: 嗯,这是我在职业生涯中别人为我做过的最好的事情之一,因为 Fortran 77 在一定程度上是基于老式打孔卡的限制的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So your lines can't go very long.
zh: 所以你的行不能太长。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's all a bit fiddly.

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't just go and put a nine.
zh: 你不能直接去加个 9。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my boss said, I reckon it would take about two weeks if you do it by hand.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 然后他给了我一本 O'Reilly Said an Orc 书。

en: And so I spent two days learning how to do regular expressions.
zh: 所以我花了两天时间学习正则表达式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I wrote a refactoring using regular expressions, accounting for line lengths and everything else.
zh: 然后我用正则表达式写了一个重构，把行长度和其他所有因素都考虑进去了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's, I think, the closest I've ever come to feeling like a god.

speaker: Unknown
en: I did it and I thought, oh, that's the thrill.
zh: 我做到了，我心想，哦，这就是那种快感。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the absolute thrill.

en: I'm not sure if it's a joke or a story, but you know, the two...

zh: 两个要砌墙的建筑工人，其中一个一块砖一块砖地开始砌墙，另一个在画画、做规划，然后，我不知道，比如，砌这堵墙要花三天，头两天这家伙什么都不干，正在砌墙的那个感觉特别好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then on day three, this builder like builds a machine that builds, or like puts together a machine that builds the wall for them and then... Yeah, but sometimes, sometimes, of course, the wall falls down the moment you set the machine.
zh: 然后到了第三天，这个家伙组装了一台能替他们砌墙的机器，然后……是的，不过有时候，有时候，当然，你刚把机器架好，墙就塌了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing is, I love that.

speaker: Unknown
en: That story, that story is all true.
zh: 我想那个业务的核心至今也基本上还是如此，当我和那些被抓……

speaker: Unknown
en: It's one of the earliest times I can remember learning something and having such a visceral reaction.
zh: 那是我记忆中最早的一次学到东西并产生如此强烈的本能反应的经历之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember just towards one of the end of the thought works, some grads in.
zh: 我记得那大概是在 ThoughtWorks 快结束的时候，有一些应届毕业生进来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're asked to tell some stories about like what had happened in previous career.
zh: 他们被要求讲一些之前职业生涯中发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I told this story.

en: I said, I added the nine, made the models bigger.

speaker: Unknown
en: And then one of the, one of the grads said, why didn't you just replace it all with a constant?
zh: 然后其中一个毕业生说，你为什么不直接把它全换成一个常量？

speaker: Unknown
en: So you could just change the number once anytime in the future.
zh: 这样以后任何时候你只需要改一次那个数字。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like,
zh: 我当时就……

speaker: Unknown
en: And I thought, I'm learning once again.
zh: 我心想，我又学到了东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's also why I love it.
zh: 这也是我热爱这行的原因之一。

en: It's like you get humbled all the time in this industry.
zh: 在这个行业里，你时时刻刻都会被打脸。

speaker: Unknown
en: You get to learn stuff.

en: Yes, there's reinvention of the wheel going on, but we're inventing better wheels the whole time.

en: And I think it's just nice to remind us every now and then I'm sure everyone who's built code and programs, like at some point you have the realization that you do feel like a god, that you can do things with these things, which is just so difficult to do by hand, right?

en: Yeah.

en: But like, it's kind of cool that we are in charge.

speaker: Unknown
en: We can do amazing stuff.

speaker: Unknown
en: So I feel a little bit more removed, but it's, yeah, talking to my son who's a programmer, he's got into it around an interesting time right now.
zh: 所以我感觉自己稍微离代码远了一点，不过，是的，和我那身为程序员的儿子聊过，他入行的时机现在看来挺有意思的。

en: And sometimes it's subjectivity, but sometimes there's something about that that you can't quite pinpoint.

zh: 去参加那样一个会议一直是我的职业愿望之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: I got to go.
zh: 我有机会去了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was after I'd written the first book and I got chatting to John Alspol there, who I still chat to for now and then.
zh: 那是在我写完第一本书之后，我在那里和 John Alspol 聊上了，我至今还时不时和他聊聊。

speaker: Unknown
en: He now works in this resilience engineering space.
zh: 他现在在韧性工程这个领域工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pointed me, I don't know if it was him or one or something else, but it pointed me at this paper by David Woods that was all about resilience engineering.
zh: 他给我指了一篇 David Woods 关于韧性工程的论文，我不确定是他还是别的什么人指的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the paper was utterly baffling to me, in absolutely no sense to me.
zh: 那篇论文对我来说完全是一头雾水，完全看不懂。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it was all, because it's not, yeah, because it's just, it's not written for computer scientists to read.
zh: 但它之所以如此，是因为它根本不是写给计算机科学家读的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm not even a computer scientist.
zh: 而我甚至都不是计算机科学家。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I was really in trouble.
zh: 所以我真的麻烦大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it was really fascinating seeing this whole other world about how people view resiliency and then what we do in the software world.
zh: 但看到这个人们看待韧性的完全不同的世界，以及我们在软件世界里的做法，真的非常引人入胜。

speaker: Unknown
en: And people like John were trying to take some of those ideas in a little bit, but I find it very difficult to take some of those ideas from sort of safety-critical systems and that type of thinking and make in any way, shape, or form palatable for normal people like me.
zh: 像 John 这样的人试图把其中一些想法引入进来一点，但我发现很难把那些来自安全关键系统之类的思想，以任何方式、形态或形式，变得让我这样的普通人能够接受。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I kind of, this has been back, what, 2016 maybe?
zh: 所以我有点……这大概是什么时候来着，2016 年？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I'd go back and try and reread that paper every six months or so, and I'd read bits around the edges and see other smarter people than me that summarized it, data better.
zh: 于是我每隔半年左右就会回去重读那篇论文，读一些相关边缘的东西，看看其他比我聪明的人总结得更好的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I was thinking, okay, these ideas now are starting to make sense.
zh: 然后我开始想，好吧，这些想法现在开始说得通了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then also I kind of realized that despite my best efforts, lots of people seem to be building microservice architectures, even though if you've read my books, most of my book is about telling you not to do it.
zh: 接着我也意识到，尽管我尽了最大努力，还是有很多人似乎在构建微服务架构，即便你读过我的书就知道，我书里大部分内容是在告诉你不要那么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you have to read the book, which is called microservices.
zh: 但你得读那本书，那本书可是叫《微服务》。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's be clear.
zh: 我们得说清楚这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: As long as they buy the book, that's the most important thing.
zh: 只要他们买了书，这才是最重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whether they read it or not, that's just, you know.
zh: 至于他们读不读，那就随他们了，你知道的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so then I realized that there are more people exposed to the horror, pain and suffering of a distributed system.
zh: 于是我意识到，有更多的人暴露在分布式系统的恐怖、痛苦和折磨之中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it was like, okay, so I've got this stuff happening.
zh: 所以就是，好吧，这些事情正在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've got this, like my, you know, my son's developing now.
zh: 我有这个，就像我的，你知道，我的这个想法正在成形。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I almost thought that...
zh: 我几乎在想……

speaker: Unknown
en: If somebody found themselves building a distributed system, working as part of building a distributed system, what was like the kind of equipment of a rubber ring I could give them, say, stay afloat and don't drown?
zh: 如果有人发现自己正在构建一个分布式系统，或者作为构建分布式系统团队的一员，我能给他们什么样的、相当于救生圈的装备，让他们说，能浮在水面别淹死？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the goal of the book is to start you off with really easy, foundational, simple kind of engineering concepts about how you can start making, dealing with the problems of the disability system, but to also take you on a journey into kind of the whole concept of resilience engineering.
zh: 所以这本书的目标是，先从非常容易的、基础性的、简单的工程概念入手，让你开始应对分布式系统(原文如此)的问题，同时也带你踏上深入韧性工程整个概念体系的旅程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it starts off with really easy ideas and then you slowly get more and more complicated.
zh: 所以它从非常简单的想法开始，然后慢慢变得越来越复杂。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, so I introduced kind of concepts like what a socio-technical system is, the difference between safety management and resilience engineering.
zh: 你知道的，我引入了像什么是社会技术系统、安全管理与韧性工程之间的区别这样的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are all like big concepts.
zh: 这些都是很大的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the second chapter after the introduction is what's observability, let's talk about OTEL.
zh: 但引言之后的第二章是什么是可观测性，我们来聊聊 OTEL。

speaker: Unknown
en: The third chapter is what's a timeout, right?
zh: 第三章是什么是超时，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And these are all, I think, quite tractable things to talk to people about.
zh: 这些都是我觉得很容易和人聊清楚的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But they're building blocks, right?
zh: 但它们是构建模块，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: The primitives for these systems and the vocabulary as well.
zh: 是这些系统的原语，也是词汇表。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, absolutely.
zh: 是的，没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to give, you know, to go through and sort of distill some of that knowledge down and also to be a bit of, I'm quite happy being a bit opinionated on these things, but I'm also lucky now because partly because of my early work, I get to chat to more people so I can actually talk to people who this is their full-time job.
zh: 而且，你知道，去梳理并把其中一些知识提炼出来，同时也作为一种……我很乐意在这些事情上带有一定观点，但我现在也很幸运，部分因为我的早期工作，我能和更多的人交流，所以我可以真正和那些以此为全职工作的人交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Trying to distill down some of that knowledge a bit.
zh: 试着把其中一些知识提炼一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I wanted that book partly as about being evergreen, but it was also about saying there are lots of people building a distributed system.
zh: 所以我写这本书，部分是希望它能长销常青，但也是想表达：有很多人在构建分布式系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's put what type of distributed system you've got off to one side for a moment.
zh: 让我们先把你构建的是哪种类型的分布式系统放到一边。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are lots of people building them, whether they should or not, and they're really important to us now.
zh: 有很多人在构建它们，不管他们该不该构建，而它们现在对我们真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how do I help people start and grow?
zh: 那么，我怎么帮助人们起步并成长呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's, that's what I wanted to do.
zh: 这就是，这就是我想做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I enjoy the process of writing anyway, but this is a book I wanted to be able to give to people.
zh: 我是说，反正我一直享受写作的过程，但这是一本我想要能够送给人们的书。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's always been why I wrote a book.
zh: 这一直是我写书的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want the books, that book, every now and then I've gone sat down to read a book, to write a book and I found someone else has done it already.
zh: 我想要书，那本书，偶尔我坐下来准备读一本书、写一本书，结果发现别人已经写过了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, well, that exists now.
zh: 就是说，好吧，这东西现在已经存在了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this for me was a book that I wanted to exist, but didn't.
zh: 所以对我来说，这是一本我希望它存在、但它并不存在的书。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's kind of why I wrote it.
zh: 这大概就是我写它的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, and I think it's a book I certainly could have used.
zh: 是啊，我觉得这肯定是一本我自己本可以用上的书。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, it got dropped into a place like Uber where we did have what I realized were distributed systems.
zh: 比如，我被扔进 Uber 这样的地方，那时我意识到我们确实有分布式系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just large systems handling a bunch of stuff, lots of services depending on one another because even a simple thing of like knowing like, oh, you should pay attention to observability that, I mean, you figure it out after a while, but it takes a while.
zh: 就只是处理一大堆东西的大型系统，很多服务相互依赖，因为哪怕是一件简单的事，比如知道「哦，你应该关注可观测性」，我是说，你过一段时间总能弄明白，但那要花不少时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's, I mean, again, I mean, maybe this is, this is my attempt to unpack some of that tacit knowledge to an extent.
zh: 而我觉得，我是说，再说一次，也许这就是，这就是我 attempt 去把那些隐性知识在一定程度上解开的一次尝试。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've made so many mistakes and I keep making mistakes.
zh: 我犯过太多错误，而且我还在不断犯错。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think making mistakes is useful, but I think also creating opportunities where people can learn from other people's mistakes first is a good idea too.
zh: 我觉得犯错是有用的，但我也认为，创造一些让人们能先从别人的错误中学习的机会，也是个好主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so in the book, I also try and pull in like real world examples and sometimes from big companies, sometimes from my mistakes to kind of make this stuff seem real.
zh: 所以在书里，我也试着引入现实世界的例子，有时来自大公司，有时来自我自己的错误，好让这些东西显得真实。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the other thing I think I really try and get across is that things go wrong.
zh: 而且我觉得我真正想传达的另一件事是，事情是会出错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, engineering is all about making sure as many things go right as possible.
zh: 我是说，工程的核心就是让尽可能多的事情顺利进行。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not about making sure everything goes right.
zh: 而不是确保一切都顺利进行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's also the only way you can build resilient systems in general is also by being honest about mistakes that have been made.
zh: 而且总的来说，构建有韧性的系统的唯一途径，也是要对已经犯过的错误保持诚实。

speaker: Unknown
en: And talking about them and sharing them because that's how everyone gets better.
zh: 去谈论它们、分享它们，因为只有这样大家才能变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you don't do that, you can't build a resilient system in your company.
zh: 如果你不这么做，你就无法在你的公司里构建一个有韧性的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this, again, is my attempt to sort of highlight all the awesome work that's gone before, the fantastic postings and reports of people that some companies share.
zh: 所以这再次是我的一次 attempt,去突出之前所有那些出色的工作、那些精彩的文章和报告，有些公司会分享这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like when there's a system that we all use or many of us use has an outage.
zh: 比如当一个我们所有人或很多人都在用的系统出现故障时。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's it's annoying, especially when you're using it.
zh: 我是说，这很烦人，尤其是当你正在用它的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I always greatly appreciate when the companies because they don't have to do this, but when they share a public postmortem or incident recap, whatever that is, they go through what happened.
zh: 但我总是非常感激那些公司——因为他们并不必须这么做——当他们分享一份公开的事后剖析或事故复盘，不管那是什么形式，他们把发生的事情讲清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, GitHub had an outage and they share that really.
zh: 比如，GitHub 出过一次故障，他们分享了那个真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Interesting one on what all the things that went wrong and in what order.
zh: 很有意思的一次，讲清楚所有出错的事情以及出错的顺序。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you also have companies where something like this happens and they don't do anything.
zh: 而你也会看到有些公司，发生了这种事却什么都不做。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, of course, you're not obliged to in any way, but I always have a bit of a lesser of...
zh: 当然，你没有任何义务这么做，但我总有点觉得……

speaker: Unknown
en: They are obliged to now, a lot of them.
zh: 他们现在有义务了，很多公司都有。

speaker: Unknown
en: Regulations are now making them.
zh: 法规现在在强制他们这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which I think is great.
zh: 我觉得这很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, things like DORA and stuff in the UK, in Europe rather.
zh: 是啊，像 DORA 之类的东西，在英国，应该说在欧洲。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there's also, we should also separate around that post-instant report stuff that there's marketing and PR versus have you done a proper post-instant review?
zh: 而且我觉得，我们还应该在这个事后报告的事情上做一个区分：营销和公关，与你是否做了一次真正的事后复盘，是两回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now I do think you've a duty of care really to let users know it's part of a proper post-instant review, but those companies that maybe say nothing, they might do a fantastic process internally.
zh: 我确实认为你有注意义务，要让用户知情，这是一次合格的事后复盘的一部分，但那些也许什么都不说的公司，他们内部可能做了非常出色的流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's also the fact that some companies that put those things out, you read them and you're like, this does feel more marketing.
zh: 还有一个事实是，有些发布这些东西的公司，你读了之后会觉得，这确实更像是营销。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a great, if you want a good, a company that puts out some of the best self-flagellating post-incident review write-ups, go for Cloudflare stuff, they absolutely go for themselves in those.
zh: 我想，如果你想要好的、一家发布了一些最「自我鞭挞式」事后复盘报告的公司，去看 Cloudflare 的东西，他们在那些报告里对自己毫不留情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, I feel like, guys, go easy on yourselves, right?
zh: 就像是，我觉得，伙计们，对自己宽容点，好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone makes some mistakes, but I quite like.
zh: 每个人都会犯一些错误，但我挺喜欢的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they did it rapidly within 24 hours, and they're a publicly traded company.
zh: 而且他们在 24 小时内就迅速做了，而且他们是一家上市公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which I think just goes back to the myth, like some of them are like, we're publicly traded, we don't want to do it because it will give away information for shareholders.
zh: 我觉得这正好回击了那个迷思，比如有些人说，我们是上市公司，我们不想做这个，因为这会向股东泄露信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, like, CloudFord does it and they're fine.
zh: 不是的，比如，CloudFord 就在做，他们也没怎么样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 正是。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also it's… And it builds up trust.
zh: 而且它是……而且这会建立信任。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is.
zh: 确实是。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, a lot of how an organization is perceived is down to how you deal with mistakes when they occur, right?
zh: 我的意思是，一个组织被如何看待，很大程度上取决于你在错误发生时如何应对，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, nothing ever goes perfectly for every company.
zh: 我的意思是，没有哪家公司会一切顺利。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in your book, you talk about the three rules of distributed systems.
zh: 所以在你的书里，你谈到了分布式系统的三条规则。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are these three rules?
zh: 这三条规则是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I really tried to distill this down because I could never remember the rule of eight that came out of Sun, the fallacies distributed computing.
zh: 所以我真的试图把这个提炼出来，因为我一直记不住 Sun 提出的八条，也就是分布式计算的谬误。

speaker: Unknown
en: I always forget what those eight were.
zh: 我总是忘记那八条是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's loads of complicated stuff, but I realized when you strip it all down, there's really only three things that really cause all the other problems.
zh: 有很多复杂的东西，但我意识到当你把它全部剥开，其实只有三件事真正导致了所有其他问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first is that you can't send information instantaneously from point A to point B.
zh: 第一是你无法把信息从 A 点瞬间发送到 B 点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's physics.
zh: 这是物理规律。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, now it turns out, when you get into it and start talking to people about quantum physics, they say, aha.
zh: 我的意思是，现在当你深入进去，开始和人们谈论量子物理时，他们会说，啊哈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there you go, there's a thing called quantum entanglement, which does allow for the theoretical instantaneous read of electron spin states across arbitrary distances.
zh: 你看，有一种东西叫量子纠缠，它确实允许在理论上跨任意距离瞬时读取电子自旋态。

speaker: Unknown
en: At which point I point out that A, that only works for reads, as far as I'm aware, and B, not a networking protocol.
zh: 这时我会指出，第一，据我所知那只适用于读取，第二，它不是一种网络协议。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like, but it takes time, right?
zh: 所以就是说，但这需要时间，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I want to get from A to B, and that, I can't control all of that.
zh: 所以我想从 A 到 B，而我无法控制这整个过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can control bits of that as a developer.
zh: 作为开发者，我可以控制其中的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I could control how much data I send.
zh: 我可以控制我发送多少数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: I could control the payload size, technology I use to serialize and deserialize.
zh: 我可以控制载荷大小、我用什么技术来序列化和反序列化。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm unlikely to be specifying the network cabling and the equipment we use or distances between them.
zh: 我不太可能去指定网络布线和我们所用的设备或它们之间的距离。

speaker: Unknown
en: So not really under my control.
zh: 所以这并不真正在我的控制之下。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the moment you go over the public internet,
zh: 而一旦你经过公共互联网，

speaker: Unknown
en: BGP has a bad day and your packet has gone down the wrong trouser leg of the internet, right?
zh: BGP 某天状态不好，你的数据包就走进了互联网错误的一条裤腿，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's the rule one.
zh: 所以这就是规则一。

speaker: Unknown
en: It takes time.
zh: 需要时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's important to recognize because sometimes it looks instantaneous, it's not.
zh: 认识到这一点很重要，因为有时它看起来是瞬时的，其实不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Second thing, sometimes the thing you want to talk to isn't there.
zh: 第二件事，有时你想通信的东西不在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes that's under, and we do things to make it under our control, right?
zh: 有时这是……而且我们会做一些事情让它处于控制之下，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we would run, say, multiple copies of a service instance behind a load balancer.
zh: 比如我们会在负载均衡器后面运行多个服务实例副本。

speaker: Unknown
en: What happens is the load balancer fails.
zh: 结果是负载均衡器故障了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I mean, like you can't control for everything, right?
zh: 我的意思是，你不可能控制一切，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I've had services taken out by a fire in the data center, a SAN caught fire, and specifically one bit of a SAN.
zh: 我遇到过服务被数据中心的一场火灾干掉，一个 SAN 着火了，具体是 SAN 的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: The SAN had a caching storage layer with SSDs, these two pairs of SSDs.
zh: 那个 SAN 有一个带 SSD 的缓存存储层，就是这两对 SSD。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the pairs of SSDs caught fire.
zh: 其中一对 SSD 着火了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other pair, the SSDs are working fine.
zh: 另一对，SSD 工作正常。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we had these weird latency graphs coming out of the SAN, like perfectly fine if your load went through the ones that weren't on fire.
zh: 所以我们从那个 SAN 里看到了这些奇怪的延迟图，如果你的负载走的是没着火的那对，就完全正常。
